title: OSM railway review policy — domain scope, eligibility and quarantine rules

domainScope.definition: An Őrszem RailwayLine represents MÁV/GYSEV infrastructure that falls under the Hungarian national network statement (VPE HÜSZ), independent of whether it currently carries passenger or freight traffic.
notExcludedByDefinition: freight-only lines that are otherwise part of the national network statement — usage=freight or an absence of passenger service is never, by itself, a reason to exclude a line
domainScope.rationale: reference-data/README.md already establishes the VPE HÜSZ network statement (annexes 5.2-4/5.2-5, published under EU Directive 2012/34/EU Art. 27) as this product's canonical definition of the Hungarian railway network. This phase reuses that definition conceptually only — no row-level content, line-code list, settlement relation or comparison result from the PENDING VPE/KTI/GYSEV dataset is used to accept, reject or reconstruct any OSM candidate. The boundary is used only to explain *why* a category of infrastructure is out of scope, never as comparison data.

candidateEligibility.syntacticValidityIsNotAcceptance: A line reference matching the pattern above is evidence eligible for review, never by itself grounds to accept a candidate as an active user-selectable RailwayLine.

automaticallyExcludedRailwayValues.handling: Never contributes an accepted candidate, and never contributes quarantine evidence — this infrastructure is not currently railway infrastructure at all. Enforced twice: by the osmium tags-filter upstream (only railway=rail|narrow_gauge is exported) and again inside build-osm-railway-reference.py, so the property never depends solely on an upstream filter.

nonOperationalTags.handling: A way carrying any of these tags never contributes an accepted candidate, regardless of its `railway` value or line reference. Its evidence is retained in non-operational-evidence.csv and, when it is a station's *only* nearby evidence, the station is quarantined under reason NON_OPERATIONAL_INFRASTRUCTURE_ONLY. A station with both ordinary and non-operational nearby evidence keeps its ordinary acceptance and still records the non-operational evidence separately — nothing is ever silently dropped.

candidateEligibility.missingOrContradictoryTagging: Defaults to quarantine. A way with an ambiguous, missing, or contradictory service/usage tag combination is treated conservatively (excluded from the accepted set) rather than guessed into either bucket.

unusualLineCodes.definition: A line code is not classified as 'unusual' by pattern alone — the policy has no separate numeric-range or suffix heuristic beyond the syntactic ref pattern above, because inventing one without a legitimate comparison source would itself be a guess. Instead, a code is flagged for mandatory manual review whenever any of its supporting evidence is NON_OPERATIONAL_INFRASTRUCTURE_ONLY, or when a reviewer's own inspection of its OSM tags/geometry raises a question that the deterministic rule cannot resolve.
unusualLineCodes.handling: Quarantine or manual decision required — never automatic acceptance or automatic rejection.

duplicateEvidenceCollapse.rule: Multiple evidence rows supporting the same accepted (kshCode, lineCode) pair are all retained as corroborating evidence, never collapsed into one row — the deterministic-acceptance rule only needs one qualifying row, but a reviewer benefits from seeing all of them. Byte-identical duplicate rows (same osm_id, ksh_code and line_code) are naturally impossible under this pipeline, since each station object is visited once.

settlementNameNormalization.rule: Strip a trailing '(vasút)állomás', 'megállóhely' or 'mh.' suffix (case-insensitively) and collapse internal whitespace. No other transliteration, casing change or diacritic normalization is applied.
settlementNameNormalization.matchingRule: EXACT string equality only, against the KSH settlement name column, after normalization above.
settlementNameNormalization.fuzzyMatchingForbidden: No similarity score, edit-distance threshold or token-overlap heuristic is used anywhere in this pipeline. A normalized OSM name that does not exactly equal exactly one KSH settlement name is quarantined under NO_UNIQUE_KSH_NAME, unconditionally.
settlementNameNormalization.whyExactMatchingIsSafe: KSH settlement names are the canonical identity this product already imports (reference-data/cleared/settlements.csv, verificationStatus VERIFIED, CC BY 4.0). An exact match against that canonical roster carries no invented similarity judgement; it either identifies the same administrative settlement or it does not.

budapestAndDistricts.kshShape: KSH lists Budapest as 23 separate district rows ('Budapest 01. ker.' .. 'Budapest 23. ker.'), never a single 'Budapest' row.
budapestAndDistricts.consequence: An OSM station literally named 'Budapest' or 'Budapest-<terminus>' (e.g. a major terminus station name) never exactly matches any KSH row under the normalization rule above, so it is always quarantined under NO_UNIQUE_KSH_NAME by default — never guessed into a specific district.
budapestAndDistricts.resolutionPath: Only a manual decision naming the specific district KSH code may accept a Budapest-area candidate, recorded exactly like any other decision (see decisions/README.md), with a human-readable note stating which district and why.

borderAndCompositeStationNames.rule: A composite or multi-settlement OSM station name (e.g. 'X-Y határállomás', 'X-Y elágazás') is handled by the same exact-match rule as any other name: if it does not equal exactly one KSH settlement name after normalization, it is quarantined under NO_UNIQUE_KSH_NAME. No splitting, no first-token heuristic, no partial matching is performed.

evidenceRequiredForAcceptance.deterministicRule: At least one ordinary (non-excluded, non-non-operational) railway way within maximumDistanceMetres of the station's point geometry, sharing a line reference that both the way and a uniquely name-matched KSH settlement can be associated with.

distanceLimit.rationale: Matches the value used to build the currently committed OSM-HU-RAIL-REVIEW-2026-09-23 snapshot; changing it requires updating this policy's version and re-running the deterministic build, never a silent parameter change.
distanceLimit.observedEvidenceDistribution: median 4.3m; 750/925 within 10m; 888/925 within 25m; 911/925 within 50m; all within the 100m hard limit.

evidenceRequiredForAcceptance.promotionAlsoRequires: A deterministically-accepted (kshCode, lineCode) pair is only a CANDIDATE. It may not appear in a promoted, importable dataset without an explicit ACCEPTED decision file (decisions/README.md) whose evidenceHash matches the candidate's current evidenceHash. This is new in this phase — the prior snapshot allowed all deterministically-accepted pairs straight into settlement-railway-lines.csv with no per-pair human decision; automaticImportAllowed being false was the only gate. That gate is preserved and a second, per-candidate gate is added on top (see promote-osm-railway-reference.py).

quarantineDefault.rule: Any candidate this policy cannot place into an unambiguous accepted-evidence bucket defaults to quarantine (NO_UNIQUE_KSH_NAME, NO_REFERENCED_LINE_WITHIN_LIMIT or NON_OPERATIONAL_INFRASTRUCTURE_ONLY). There is no code path in build-osm-railway-reference.py that accepts a candidate outside the deterministic rule above.

staleDecisionProtection.rule: Every candidate in candidates.json carries an evidenceHash computed deterministically from the exact evidence rows that produced it (OSM object ids, distances, tags). A decision file's own recorded evidenceHash must match the candidate's current evidenceHash at promotion time; a mismatch means the underlying source data changed since the decision was made, and the decision is void — the candidate reverts to requiring a fresh manual decision. See promote-osm-railway-reference.py.

whatStillRequiresExplicitHumanApproval: Every accepted (kshCode, lineCode) pair candidate, regardless of how confidently the deterministic rule accepted it — a machine rule proposes, a human decision promotes.

Every NON_OPERATIONAL_INFRASTRUCTURE_ONLY quarantine entry, if a reviewer believes local evidence actually does justify treating a specific object as network-statement infrastructure (this policy's default is to never auto-accept these; only an explicit ACCEPTED decision, with a documented legitimate source, can override the default).

The overall dataset promotion: verificationStatus may only become VERIFIED, and automaticImportAllowed/runtimeCompatible may only become true, through the promotion command, never through this build script.
